### Will you contribute a fix?

No — reporting for maintainers to handle

### Bug Summary

On Linux (fresh AppImage installation of Termul v0.4.52), typing `@` or `@<filename>` in the agent chat composer fails to find any files or folders, displaying `"No files or folders match. Try another name."` despite valid files existing directly in the active project directory (visible in the file explorer).

Inspection of the logs reveals that ripgrep (`rg`) crashes immediately with `ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(139))` (SIGSEGV - segmentation fault) whenever `useComposerMentions` triggers `search_file_names_stream`. In addition, child processes like `node` fail to load bundled libraries (`LIBFFI_CALL_PLAN_8.4 not found` in `/tmp/.mount_TermulXXXXXX/usr/lib/libffi.so.8`), indicating that AppImage `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` inheritance pollutes spawned subprocesses and leads to library incompatibilities/segfaults on modern Linux distributions.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install and launch Termul v0.4.52 via AppImage on Linux (CachyOS / Arch Linux).
2. Create or open a project workspace by selecting a project folder with files (e.g. containing `README.md`, `setup.sh`, etc.).
3. Open an Agent Chat tab (e.g. ACP / Gemini / Claude session).
4. In the chat composer input, type `@` or `@README`.
5. Observe: The autocomplete dropdown shows: `"No files or folders match. Try another name."`.
6. Check `termul.log`: Multiple warnings are recorded:
   `[frontend] [useComposerMentions] composer mention search done with error: code=RG_STREAM_FAILED error=rg exited with status: ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(139))`

### Environment

- **OS:** CachyOS x86_64 (Kernel: Linux 7.2.7-1-cachyos)
- **Desktop Environment:** KDE Plasma 6.7.5 / KWin (Wayland)
- **Termul version:** Termul v0.4.52
- **Install method:** AppImage
- **Hardware / Host:** HyperX OMEN Gaming Laptop 15-gb0xxx, AMD Ryzen 5 240 (12) @ 5.02 GHz, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5050 Max-Q / AMD Radeon 760M, 32GB RAM

### Logs, Errors, or Screenshots

Related node spawn failure showing AppImage mount path library pollution:
```shell
[2026-10-19][05:02:35][termul_manager_lib::acp::manager::stderr_ring][WARN] [acp] spawn failed: kind=acp-registry:codex-acp command=npx detail=agent failed to start: Internal error: {
  "spawned_at": "/home/runner/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/agent-client-protocol-1.3.0/src/jsonrpc.rs:1524:39",
  "data": "Process exited with exit status: 1: node: /tmp/.mount_TermulkGHjLf/usr/lib/libffi.so.8: version `LIBFFI_CALL_PLAN_8.4' not found (required by node)\n"
}
agent stderr tail:
node: /tmp/.mount_TermulkGHjLf/usr/lib/libffi.so.8: version `LIBFFI_CALL_PLAN_8.4' not found (required by node)
```

**2. Screenshot:**
![Termul File Mention Search Error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KazamiHazaki/oraoraoraora/main/assets/termul/termul-at-mention-file-search-error.png)

### Additional Context

- Wait status `139` is `128 + 11` (SIGSEGV / segmentation fault).
- When running from an AppImage on Linux, AppImage sets `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to include `$APPDIR/usr/lib`. When Termul spawns external binaries like `rg` (or ACP agents via `node`/`npx`), these child processes inherit the AppImage's `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. On modern Linux distros (e.g. CachyOS with glibc 2.41 / libffi 3.4.x), this leads to ABI collisions, missing symbols, and crashes.
- Child command execution in Rust (`Command::new`) should consider stripping or resetting `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (or restoring the original host environment) before spawning sidecars and external tooling so they use the correct host runtime libraries.
title: [Bug]: File @-mention in agent chat fails ("No files or folders match") due to ripgrep crash (SIGSEGV / status 139) on Linux AppImage

body:
## Bug Description

Clicking an external link in an agent chat shows a confirmation modal ("open this link?"), but **the link already opens in the system browser before the user confirms**. The modal appears *after* the browser has already launched, making the confirmation pointless.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an agent chat with a message containing an external link.
2. Click the link.
3. Observe: the confirmation modal appears **and** the link opens in the system browser at the same time (or the browser opens first).

## Expected Behavior

Clicking the link shows the confirmation modal first. The link only opens in the system browser **after** the user clicks "Open" (or equivalent confirm action) in the modal.

## Actual Behavior

The link opens in the system browser immediately on click, without waiting for the user's confirmation. The modal appears as an afterthought.

## Environment

- Termul version: v0.4.52
- OS: Windows 11

## Notes

This is a regression of the fix for #406 (closed: clicking a link navigates the whole app away). The confirmation modal was added, but the link-opening is not gated behind it — the `window.open` / `shell.open` call fires before or alongside the modal instead of after confirmation.
title: [Bug]: External link in agent chat opens in system browser before the confirmation modal is answered

body:
## Summary

When a chat is reopened through any path other than **Reload this chat**, Termul resumes the ACP session without an MCP server list. The new agent process starts with no MCP servers. That includes the host `termul` server, which provides the canvas tools, `plan`, `set_session_title` and `ask_user`, and every MCP server the user configured in Termul. The agent loses these tools in the middle of the conversation.

## Reproduction

1. Start a Claude Agent chat in a project with Termul Canvas open. Use canvas tools, for example `create_node` or `screenshot`. They work.
2. Leave the chat idle until the host idle reaper stops it.
3. Type a new message. `idleStopAutoResume` resumes the chat on the new input.
4. Ask the agent to use a canvas tool.

**Expected:** the canvas tools and the configured MCP servers are still available.
**Actual:** the agent reports that `mcp__termul__*` (and pencil, context7, unityMCP, blender) were "removed from the configuration". Canvas export and edits are no longer possible in that chat.

## Evidence (termul.log, 2026-10-19, session 1ac26dee…)

```
02:13:52 [PtyManager] App window hidden
02:15:10 [PtyManager] App window visible
02:15:30 [frontend] [AgentChatPanel.idleStopAutoResume] Resuming stopped chat 1ac26dee-… on user input
02:15:31 connection; name="termul-acp-6e6f83bc-…"          <- fresh agent process
02:15:32 [acp] agent 6e6f83bc-… spawned
```

There is no `[acp] session … reopen attaches N mcp servers` line, so `prepare_reopen_mcp` received `None`.

## Root cause

- `src/renderer/components/chat/use-idle-stop-auto-resume.ts` calls `openHistorySession(sessionId)` with no options.
- `src/renderer/stores/acp-store/slices/session.ts` (`loadSession` / `resumeSession` calls around L1154, L1218, L1259) forwards `options?.mcpServers`, which is `undefined` here.
- `src/renderer/lib/acp-transport/types.ts` documents this as intended: "`mcpServers` is set only by Reload this chat … Omitted keeps a normal history reopen."
- `src-tauri/src/acp/manager/mod.rs` `prepare_reopen_mcp`: `None` means no client MCP list and no host plan server.

Only `reloadAgentChat` (`src/renderer/stores/reload-chat.ts`) builds the list with `selectMcpServersForAgent(...)`. The same gap probably affects opening a past chat from the sidebar onto a fresh process, and other reopen paths that spawn a new agent.

## Suggested fix

When a reopen runs on a fresh agent process (idle-stop auto-resume, manual "Resume chat", history open), pass `selectMcpServersForAgent(state.mcpServers, capabilities).servers`, as reload does. The simplest version: `openHistorySession` defaults `mcpServers` to that list when the caller omits it. Then update the `ReopenCallOptions` doc comment. Add a test that idle-stop auto-resume sends a non-`undefined` `mcpServers` on `resumeSession`.

## Workaround

Use **Reload this chat** after a chat comes back from an idle stop. That path reattaches the MCP servers.
title: Idle-stop auto-resume (and other non-reload reopens) drop all MCP servers, including Termul Canvas
